turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I'm having this issue with eating, mostly at night. 

Once I start eating, it's like I just lose control. It's a strange feeling because it feels like I can actually see myself doing it, and in my head, I'm telling myself to just stop. But my hands just keep going back for more. I just can't seem to make myself stop once I get going.

symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient explicitly describes losing control while eating at night, unable to stop despite mentally telling themselves to do so.

turns.doctor_question: After these episodes where you can't stop eating, do you do anything to try to counteract or undo what you've eaten, such as making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
turns.patient_response:
I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives, no. But I do try to make up for it. 

After a bad eating night, I’ll usually tell myself I’m evening things out by just skipping breakfast and lunch the next day. And I'll push the exercise. I'll go out and walk miles past my usual route to try and burn it off... even when my knees are aching and telling me I really should just head home. I just feel like I have to undo it somehow.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient describes engaging in non-purging compensatory behaviors after eating episodes, specifically skipping breakfast and lunch and exercising excessively despite physical pain.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies engaging in purging behaviors such as self-induced vomiting or using laxatives.

turns.doctor_question: When you're eating during these nighttime episodes, do you feel like you're eating much larger amounts of food than most people would eat in a similar situation, and do you feel a sense of loss of control during that time?
turns.patient_response:
Yes, it's definitely a lot more than anyone would normally eat. And like I said, I completely lose control once I start. 

Some evenings, I’ll start off just having some leftovers. But then... I just keep going. I'll end up making sandwiches, eating bowls of cereal, cookies, just whatever snack food is sitting in the pantry. It ends up being far, far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper.

symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly confirms eating definitely a lot more food than normal, describing consuming leftovers, sandwiches, cereal, and cookies in amounts far exceeding a normal meal.
symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient explicitly states that they completely lose control once they start eating.

turns.doctor_question: How often would you say these episodes of overeating happen—are we talking about a few times a week, multiple times a week, or how frequently?
turns.patient_response: Well, for the last several months, I'd say most weeks have at least one night where I eat like that. And then... well, I spend the whole next day trying to make up for it. I'll skip meals, set really strict rules for myself about what I'm allowed to eat, or go out and take one of those extra-long walks I mentioned. So, yeah, at least once a week.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in non-purging compensatory behaviors, such as skipping meals and taking extra-long walks, to make up for episodes of overeating.

turns.doctor_question: How do these eating episodes and the way you try to compensate for them affect your daily life—do they cause you emotional distress, or interfere with work, school, relationships, or other important activities?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'm still managing my job and my basic responsibilities just fine. But... it does affect me, mostly socially. I've been turning down plans lately, like going to the theater or meeting up with my walking club. I just feel so ashamed of it all. I get preoccupied with worrying about how I look, whether people think I look disciplined enough, or if they can tell what I'm doing. So, I just end up isolating myself instead.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned you don't make yourself vomit or use laxatives. But I want to be thorough—have you ever used any other methods to try to get rid of food after these episodes, such as enemas, diuretics, or anything else like that?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't done anything like that. I don't use enemas or diuretics or any kind of pills. Like I said, it's mostly just skipping meals the next day, restricting what I eat, or going for those long walks to try and burn it off. That's really all I do to try and make up for it.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in non-purging compensatory behaviors to make up for eating episodes, specifically skipping meals, restricting food, and going on long walks to burn calories.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies any purging behaviors, stating they have never used enemas, diuretics, or any pills to get rid of food.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned these episodes have been happening for several months now. Can you tell me approximately when they first started—how long ago would you say this pattern began?
turns.patient_response: I'd say it's been going on for about four months now. It... well, it started right around the time a good friend of mine died. After he passed, my evenings just stopped feeling organized. I didn't really have that structure anymore, and I guess that's when this whole pattern really began.

turns.doctor_question: During these nighttime eating episodes, do you experience any emotional distress—like anxiety, guilt, or shame—while you're actually eating, or does the distress mainly come afterward when you realize how much you've eaten?
turns.patient_response: Well, while I'm actually eating... I don't really know if I'm feeling much of anything. It's almost like I just zone out. The guilt and the shame, that mostly hits me afterward. Once I stop and actually realize how much I just ate, that's when I feel really terrible about it.

symptom_reasoning.S055: The patient explicitly confirms feeling strong guilt, shame, and feeling 'really terrible' afterward upon realizing how much they ate.

turns.doctor_question: When you restrict your eating the day after an episode—skipping breakfast and lunch—is that the main way you try to compensate, or do you also do things like taking diet pills, using supplements, or any other methods to control your weight that we haven't discussed yet?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't take any diet pills or supplements or anything like that. It's really just what I mentioned—skipping breakfast and lunch, and then going for those walks. That's the only way I try to handle it. I don't do anything else.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient confirms engaging in non-purging compensatory behaviors to handle eating episodes, specifically skipping meals (breakfast and lunch) and going for walks.
